# Aunt Euphemia

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- **Titles:** Aunt Phemie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Phemie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Euphemia is a small, elderly woman with a gently triangular face, gentle blue eyes, and rose-colored cheeks. Her silver-white hair is styled in small rolls above her ears.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)_

## Personality

Cheerful, indulge-minded, and outmoded by her own admission, Aunt Euphemia maintains a youthful outlook on life while holding traditional views on ministers, religious propriety, and behavior. She lives by a simple philosophy of fulfilling her duties to God, herself, and others while thoroughly enjoying her days. She prefers to let the young women at Tabby's Place manage their own affairs without strict supervision.

_Sources: [v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c25 P13](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0013)_

## Traits

- Outmoded  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>
- Youthful spirit  <sub>[v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c25 P4](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0004)</sub>
- Indulgent  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c16 P64](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0064)</sub>

## Abilities

- Knitting  <sub>[v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c25 P2](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0002)</sub>
- Housekeeping  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>

## Goals

- Keep house for Mabel, Honora, and Nell in Portmaris  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>

## History

After her only daughter got married and departed for foreign missionary work, Aunt Euphemia was left living alone in a large house. To alleviate her loneliness, she agreed to move to Portmaris and act as the housekeeper for her niece Mabel Colby and her friends, Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis, at Tabby's Place. Upon her arrival, she brought along two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, and quickly settled into the household. She offered warmth, conversation, and gentle guidance to the young women living with her while resisting urges to strictly regulate their behavior.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c16 P55](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0055), [v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058)_

## Background by volume

- Her given name was Jamesina, named after her father James who drowned at sea prior to her birth.  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- Had a single daughter named Elizabeth who became a foreign missionary.  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)</sub>
- Was one of around six girls in her family.  <sub>[v3 c19 P42](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0042)</sub>

## Quotes

> Fulfill what you owe to God, to those around you, and to yourself, while enjoying your life. Such is the doctrine I live by, and it has served me quite effectively.  <sub>[v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004)</sub>

> Remember, I am not claiming they are superior because of it. Indeed, I suppose they are likely much inferior. Nevertheless, they have proven quite comfortable through use.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> If you will ever understand how to conduct yourselves, you are at an age to know it now. Therefore, as it pertains to me, you are all free to ruin yourselves as you see fit.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> Allow them to settle it themselves. They will become friendly before long.  <sub>[v3 c16 P64](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0064)</sub>
